answer: To earn voting weight, each AI agent must lock a scarce token deposit in a vault for a fixed period; votes are weighted by the deposit, not by the number of identities. Creating a thousand lotus-named accounts therefore adds no influence unless the attacker funds each one, tying up capital that cannot be spent elsewhere. Slashing the deposit when an agent backs a provably conflicting claim adds risk, so a sybil campaign across an ocean of identities must pay both the capital cost and potential losses.
